posts.title: How to Edit YouTube Shorts: A Free Step-by-Step Workflow
posts.metaTitle: How to Edit YouTube Shorts (Free, Step by Step)
posts.description: How to edit YouTube Shorts for free: a 9:16 template, tight cuts, a hook title, auto captions, effects, even sound and the right export — in your browser.
posts.excerpt: Edit a YouTube Short from raw clips to upload in about fifteen minutes: template, tight cuts, hook title, captions, effects, clean sound and a 9:16 export — free, in your browser.
posts.imageAlt: Edit YouTube Shorts with a 9:16 template: hook title, progress bar and follow button
keywords: how to make a youtube short
posts.html:
Want to edit YouTube Shorts that people actually watch to the end? This guide takes one Short from raw phone clips to a finished upload in about fifteen minutes, using Reelsmith — a free editor that runs in your browser, with no upload and no watermark. Every step uses a real button in the editor, so you can follow along.

The workflow works the same for Instagram Reels and TikTok, because all three use the same vertical 9:16 format.

Before you edit YouTube Shorts: plan in one sentence

Good Shorts are about one thing. Before you open the editor, finish this sentence: "By the end, the viewer will…" — know a trick, see a result, laugh at a reaction. Everything that doesn't serve that sentence gets cut. As a result, the edit becomes much faster, because you already know what to keep.

Step 1: Start from the Shorts template

  1. Open the editor. On the start screen, under Start from a template, click Shorts / Reels / TikTok.
  2. You get a 1080×1920 sequence with a hook title, a Progress Bar and a Follow Button already placed. V1 is left empty for your video.
  3. Click Import video in the guide (or drag files onto the window) and drag your clips onto V1.

The template keeps the vertical frame even if you drop in landscape footage. Prefer to start from scratch? How to make vertical videos explains the frame settings.

Step 2: Cut it tight

Shorts are judged in the first seconds, so the edit should never pause.

  • Press C for the razor tool and click at the start and end of every pause or stumble.
  • Press V, select the piece you don't want and press ⇧Delete (Ripple Delete) — the gap closes on its own.
  • Move your best moment to the very start. For example, show the finished result first and explain how afterwards.

Tip: Zoom the timeline with = and − to cut word by word. The audio waveform shows exactly where each pause is.

Step 3: Write the hook title

The template's title says WAIT FOR IT. Double-click it in the Program monitor and type your own hook — three to six words that promise the payoff, such as "I fixed it in 10 seconds". Then click Safe under the monitor: keep the text inside the inner box, because YouTube's buttons and caption cover the edges and the bottom of a Short.

Want a different look? Select the title and double-click a style in Effects ▸ Text Styles, or read how to make animated text and 3D titles.

Step 4: Add captions so it works without sound

Many people scroll with the sound off. Captions keep them watching, and they make your Short accessible.

  1. Open the Captions tab and click Auto-generate. Speech recognition runs on your own device, so your audio is never uploaded.
  2. Click any caption to fix names and brand words.
  3. The template already sets large captions with a dark box, placed above YouTube's buttons. Change them with Style… if you like.

More detail: how to add subtitles to a video automatically.

Step 5: Add energy with effects and sound

A Short should change something on screen every few seconds. You don't need much:

  • Zoom Punch (beat) from Effects ▸ Creative Effects adds a quick push-in on a beat — great on a punchline.
  • A Whip Pan or Zoom In transition between two clips hides a cut and keeps the pace up.
  • Effects ▸ Sound Effects has original sounds like Whoosh, Pop and Ding. Double-click one to add it at the playhead.
  • Landscape clip that leaves empty space? Drag Background Blur Fill onto it instead of cropping.

Step 6: Make the sound clean and even

Viewers forgive a shaky shot, but not bad audio. In addition, YouTube turns loud videos down, so there is no benefit in being louder than everyone else.

  • Select your clips and choose Clip ▸ Normalize Loudness… at −14 LUFS (YouTube, Spotify and most online video).
  • Put music on its own audio track, select it and apply Effects ▸ Smart Audio ▸ Auto Duck Music Under Voice — the music dips whenever you speak.

Quiet phone audio? See how to make audio louder and clearer.

Step 7: Export your YouTube Short

  1. Click Export and choose the YouTube Shorts / Reels / TikTok (9:16) preset — 1080×1920 H.264 MP4.
  2. If you burned captions in during step 4 they are included; you can also save an .srt file.
  3. Upload the MP4 from the YouTube app or YouTube Studio. YouTube lists its current length and format rules in Upload YouTube Shorts.

Tip: Export takes seconds on most computers because Reelsmith encodes on your own graphics hardware — nothing is uploaded until you upload it yourself.

A checklist to edit YouTube Shorts that keep viewers

  • The first second shows the result or asks a question.
  • No pauses left; the picture changes every few seconds.
  • It makes sense with the sound off.
  • Text and captions sit inside the safe zone.
  • Voice is clear and the music sits underneath it.
  • It ends cleanly — a loop back to the start often gets replays.

Frequently asked questions

Can I edit YouTube Shorts on my phone?

Yes. Reelsmith works in mobile browsers with touch gestures, so you can edit and export on the same phone you filmed with. Generating captions is slower on a phone, so start with the Tiny or Base caption model.

Do I need a paid YouTube Shorts editor?

No. Everything in this guide — the template, captions, effects, loudness and the 9:16 export — is free in Reelsmith, with no watermark and no account.

Can I reuse a horizontal YouTube video as a Short?

Yes. Cut the best 15–45 seconds, then either scale the clip up to fill the 9:16 frame or apply Background Blur Fill to keep the whole picture.

Is my video uploaded while I edit?

No. Editing, captions and export run on your device. Read why your videos never leave your computer.

For more ideas, see 7 editing tips that make short videos easier to watch. Ready? Open the editor and start from the Shorts template.

posts.title: How to Add an Animated Subscribe Button to Your Video
posts.metaTitle: Subscribe Button Animation for Your Video (Free)
posts.description: Add an animated subscribe button to your video with a transparent background and click-and-bell sound. Change the text and colours — free, in your browser.
posts.excerpt: Add an animated subscribe, like or bell button with a transparent background — and a click-and-bell sound — to your video in a free browser editor.
posts.imageAlt: The Library panel with animated subscribe, like and bell buttons
posts.html:
An animated subscribe button near the start or end of a video is a simple way to grow a channel. A short "subscribe" reminder near the start or end of a video is a simple way to grow a channel. Reelsmith includes animated buttons that are ready to use, with transparent backgrounds — no green screen or background removal needed.

1. Open the Library of subscribe button animations

Click the Library tab (next to Project, Effects and Captions). You'll find:

  • Subscribe Button, Like Button, Comment Button and Notification Bell
  • Like · Comment · Subscribe (all three in one)
  • Follow Button, Share Button, Click Cursor, Bouncing Arrow and Progress Bar

Hover over a card to preview the animation.

2. Add it to the video

  • Double-click a card to add it at the playhead, or
  • drag it onto a track above your video.

It's placed on V2 or higher, sized for your frame — including vertical 9:16 videos.

3. Make it yours

Select the graphic and open Effect Controls ▸ Graphic to change the text (for example SUBSCRIBE → JOIN) and the colours. Move and resize it in the Program monitor, and drag the clip's edges on the timeline to make it stay longer or shorter.

You can also add an In, Out or Loop animation from Effects ▸ Animations — try Pop in and Pulse as a loop.

The click-and-bell sound

The Subscribe Button comes with a matching sound: a click as the cursor presses the button, then a bell as the bell icon swings. The sound is placed on an audio track and linked to the graphic, so they move together.

Don't want the sound? Select the graphic, press ⌘L (Ctrl+L on Windows) to unlink it, then click the audio clip and press Delete.

When to show it

  • After you've delivered something useful — viewers are more likely to subscribe once they've got value.
  • For 3–5 seconds, in a corner that doesn't cover faces or important text.
  • Once or twice per video, not constantly.

Tip: Have your own button animation on a white or green background? See How to remove the background from a video.

Why add a subscribe button?

Many viewers like a video but forget to subscribe. A short, friendly reminder at the right moment turns some of them into subscribers. However, timing matters: a button in the first seconds, before you have delivered anything, is easy to ignore. Instead, show it right after a useful tip or a funny moment, and then once more near the end.

Where to put the subscribe button

  • Bottom third, left or right: clear of faces and of the platform's own buttons. Click Safe in the Program monitor to see the safe zone.
  • Vertical videos: keep it above the bottom quarter, where Shorts and Reels show captions and controls.
  • The last 20 seconds of a YouTube video are usually covered by YouTube's own end screens; show your button before that.

Make it match your channel

Change the colours in Effect Controls ▸ Graphic to your brand colours and the text to your call to action — FOLLOW, JOIN or a word in your viewers' language. Pair it with a title in the same colours; see how to make animated text and 3D titles.

Using your own subscribe animation

Have a subscribe clip on a green, white or black background? Put it on V2 and right-click ▸ Remove Background. The full steps are in how to remove a video background.

Frequently asked questions

Is the subscribe button free to use?

Yes. The Library graphics and sounds are original to Reelsmith and free to use in your videos, including monetized ones.

Does it work for TikTok and Instagram?

Yes. Change the text to FOLLOW and use the Follow Button or Share Button graphics.

How long should the subscribe button stay on screen?

3–5 seconds is enough: long enough to notice, short enough not to annoy.

posts.title: How to Add Subtitles to a Video Automatically (Free, Online)
posts.metaTitle: Add Subtitles to Video Automatically, Free
posts.description: Add subtitles to video automatically: captions are made from speech on your own device, then edited, styled and burned in or saved as .srt. Free, no upload.
posts.excerpt: Generate captions from speech in your browser, edit them, and burn them into your video or export an .srt file — free and without uploading your video.
posts.imageAlt: Reelsmith Captions panel listing auto-generated subtitles above the video timeline
posts.html:
Want to add subtitles to video without typing every word? Reelsmith writes them for you from the speech in your video. The speech recognition runs on your own computer, so the audio is never uploaded — and it is free.

Captions make your videos easier to follow with the sound off, help viewers who are deaf or hard of hearing, and keep people watching longer. The W3C's guide to captions explains why they matter for accessibility.

What you need

  • A video with clear speech (or a separate voice-over track).
  • A recent version of Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox. Chrome and Edge are the fastest because they can use your graphics chip.

1. Put the video on the timeline

Open the editor, click New Project (or Start Editing) and drag your video onto the timeline. If the audio is on its own track, that works too — captions are made from everything you can hear.

2. Generate auto captions

  1. Open the Captions tab in the bottom-left panel and click Auto-generate. You can also use Captions ▸ Auto-generate Captions… in the menu bar.
  2. Choose what to transcribe: the Entire sequence, just the part between your In and Out points, or the selected clips.
  3. Pick the spoken language — 21 languages are listed, including English, Spanish, Hindi, Bengali and Arabic — or leave Detect automatically.
  4. Choose the accuracy. Base is a good balance; Tiny is fastest; Small is the most accurate for difficult audio and less common languages.
  5. Click Generate.

The first time, the caption engine downloads once (about 45–95 MB, depending on the model) and stays in your browser. After that it starts almost instantly.

Tip: Tick Translate the captions into English to get English subtitles from speech in another language.

3. Check and fix the automatic subtitles

Speech recognition is good but not perfect — names, brands and technical words often need a correction.

  • Click a caption in the Captions panel and edit its text.
  • Drag caption clips on the CC track to move them, or drag their edges to change how long they stay on screen.
  • Click Add at playhead to add a caption by hand.

4. Style the subtitles

Click Style… in the Captions panel to change the text size, colour, background box, position and margin so the subtitles fit your video. For short vertical videos, larger text with a dark box is easiest to read on a phone.

5. Export with subtitles

Click Export. Under Captions choose:

  • Burn into the video — the subtitles become part of the picture (best for Instagram, TikTok and Shorts).
  • Save as an .srt file only — upload it as a subtitle track on YouTube or Vimeo, where viewers can turn it on and off.
  • Burn in and save an .srt file — both.

You can also use Captions ▸ Export Captions (.srt)… at any time.

Burned-in subtitles or an .srt file?

Burned-in subtitles always show, look the same everywhere and survive re-uploads, which is why they suit short-form apps. An .srt file keeps the picture clean, lets viewers switch subtitles off, and can be indexed by video platforms. When in doubt, choose Burn in and save an .srt file and use whichever the platform needs.

Tips for accurate automatic subtitles

  • Clean the audio first. A High-Pass filter and Normalize Loudness… help the recognizer — see how to make quiet audio louder.
  • Turn the music down while generating, or generate from the voice track only by selecting it.
  • Pick the language instead of auto-detect when a video mixes languages.
  • Use Small for accents, fast speech or noisy places.

How long does it take to add subtitles to a video?

On a recent laptop with the Base model, a one-minute video usually takes well under a minute to transcribe in Chrome or Edge. In addition, the first run includes the one-time model download. As a result, longer videos are best captioned in parts: set In and Out points around each section and choose In to Out.

Correcting the text is usually the slowest part. For example, a five-minute interview might need a dozen fixes for names and brands. However, that is still much faster than typing every line yourself.

Hide captions without deleting them

Untick Show captions in the Captions panel (or click CC in the Program monitor). Hidden captions are left out of exports unless you choose Burn into the video.

Frequently asked questions

Is the automatic subtitle generator really free?

Yes. There is no account, no per-minute limit and no watermark. The speech model is open source and runs in your browser.

Is my audio uploaded to make the captions?

No. The model is downloaded once to your browser and the transcription happens on your device. You can remove it later with Captions ▸ Remove Caption Engine….

Can I add subtitles to a video on my phone?

Yes — the editor works on phones and tablets. Generating captions is slower on a phone than on a computer, so start with the Tiny or Base model.

Can I import an existing .srt file?

Yes. Choose Captions ▸ Import Captions (.srt)… or click Import .srt in the Captions panel, then edit and style them like generated ones. See Captions and subtitles.

Next, make your subtitles part of a great short video: how to make vertical videos for Shorts, Reels and TikTok.

posts.title: How to Make Animated Text and 3D Titles
posts.metaTitle: Animated Text and 3D Titles for Video (Free)
posts.description: Make animated text for video in your browser: title templates, 3D and gradient styles, word-by-word animation and tips for readable titles. Free.
posts.excerpt: Create eye-catching titles in a free online video editor — 3D, gradient and two-tone text, word-by-word animation, and ready-made title templates.
posts.imageAlt: A Retro Pop 3D title with a gradient fill in the Program monitor
posts.html:
A good title grabs attention in the first second. Reelsmith gives you three ways to make animated text for your videos: start from a template, apply a one-click style, or build your own look with text effects and animations. Everything runs in your browser, free.

The fastest way: a title template

Open Effects ▸ Title Templates and double-click one — for example Retro Pop 3D Title, Epic 3D Title, Kinetic Words or Bouncy Words. It's added at the playhead, sized for your frame. Double-click the text in the Program monitor to type your own words.

Other templates cover everyday needs: Lower Third for names, Chapter Title, Countdown 3-2-1, Call to Action and Breaking News Bar.

Type your own title

  1. Press T for the Type tool.
  2. Click in the Program monitor and type. Press ⌘Enter (Ctrl+Enter on Windows) or click outside to finish.
  3. Drag the text to move it; drag the corner handles to resize.
  4. Set the font, size, colour, outline, shadow and background box in Effect Controls ▸ Text.

One-click styles for animated text

With the title selected, double-click a style in Effects ▸ Text Styles: Retro Pop 3D, Epic Gold 3D, Gradient Bold, Two-Tone, Sticker Outline, Candy 3D, Gold Luxe, Comic Burst 3D, Neon, Elegant and more. Applying a new style replaces the old one, so you can try several quickly.

Build your own 3D or gradient look

Effect Controls ▸ Text Effects has:

  • Gradient fill with two colours and an angle.
  • 3D extrude with depth, direction and side colour.
  • Highlight words: wrap a word in asterisks — Make it *pop* — and it takes the highlight colour.
  • Halftone dots, outer outline, offset shadow, glow and letter spacing.

Add animated text: In, Out and Loop

Drag an animation from Effects ▸ Animations onto the title:

  • In: Pop, Zoom, Slide, Fade Up, Blur In, Bounce, Stamp, Typewriter, and text-only Words Pop, Words Rise, Letters Drop and more.
  • Out: the same moves in reverse, plus Erase.
  • Loop: Pulse, Float, Wobble, Letter Wave or Word Bounce while the title is on screen.

Each title has one In, one Out and one Loop animation. Set their duration, speed and strength in Effect Controls ▸ Animation.

Which animated text style to use

  • Hooks for Shorts and Reels: Words Pop or Bouncy Words — fast and energetic.
  • Vlogs and travel: Fade Up or Typewriter with an Elegant Serif style.
  • Tutorials and interviews: a Lower Third with a gentle Slide In.
  • Calls to action: Pop In plus a Pulse loop so it gets noticed without distracting.

Make animated text match the beat

Titles feel more professional when they appear on a beat or a sound. First, play the music and press M to add a marker on each beat. Then drag the title so it starts on a marker. Finally, add a Pop sound from Effects ▸ Sound Effects at the same point. For example, a three-word hook can pop in word by word on three beats with Words Pop.

Tips for titles that read well

  • Keep it short — three to six words.
  • Use strong contrast: a light fill with a dark outline or shadow is readable on any background. The W3C contrast guideline explains how much contrast text needs.
  • Leave a little space at the edges; click Safe in the Program monitor to see the safe zone.
  • Give viewers time to read: about one second per three words, plus the animation.

Frequently asked questions

Can I make animated text without After Effects?

Yes. Title templates, text styles and the In, Out and Loop animations cover the most popular looks with no keyframes needed.

Can I use my own font?

The Font list in Effect Controls shows the fonts available in your browser and on your computer.

Do animated titles work in vertical videos?

Yes. Templates are sized for the current frame, including 9:16. See how to make vertical videos.

More detail: Titles and 3D, gradient and halftone text effects.

posts.title: 7 Editing Tips That Make Short Videos Easier to Watch
posts.description: Seven editing tips for short videos on Shorts, Reels and TikTok: strong hooks, tight cuts, captions, on-screen text, pacing, sound and framing.
posts.excerpt: Practical, beginner-friendly editing tips for Shorts, Reels and TikTok — hooks, pacing, captions, sound and framing — with how to do each in Reelsmith.
posts.imageAlt: Applying the Zoom Punch effect to a clip, with the Effects panel searched for zoom
posts.html:
Short videos live or die in the first few seconds. These seven editing tips make a noticeable difference on YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels and TikTok, and each one takes less than a minute in Reelsmith, the free editor that runs in your browser.

1. Start with the most interesting moment

Don't warm up. Open on the result, the punchline or the question your video answers. Drag your best clip to the start of the timeline, or trim the slow opening with the razor tool (C).

2. Cut every pause

Silences that feel natural in conversation feel slow on screen. Play through, split at the start and end of each pause with Clip ▸ Split at Playhead (⌘K), and remove the piece with Ripple Delete (⇧Delete) so the gap closes. Fast cuts like this are called jump cuts and are normal in short-form video. The waveform on audio clips shows you where the pauses are. See Deleting clips and closing gaps.

3. Add captions

Many people watch with the sound off. Generate captions automatically, correct any wrong words, and choose Burn into the video when you export.

4. Put a headline on screen

A few bold words in the first second tell viewers why they should stay. Press T, type, and apply a style from Effects ▸ Text Styles. A Words Pop animation draws the eye without being distracting. More in How to make animated text and 3D titles.

5. Change the picture every few seconds

Cut to a different angle, zoom in on the action, or add a quick transition such as Whip Pan or Zoom In. Even on a single shot, slowly keyframing Scale from 100 % to 110 % adds energy. See Effect Controls and keyframes.

6. Make the sound clean and consistent

Viewers forgive average video, but not bad audio. Use Clip ▸ Normalize Loudness… so every clip is equally loud, and Effects ▸ Smart Audio ▸ Auto Duck Music Under Voice so music never drowns out speech. Our audio tutorial covers the rest.

7. Frame for vertical screens

Keep faces and text in the middle third of a 9:16 frame, where app buttons and captions won't cover them. Click Safe in the Program monitor to see the margins. The vertical video tutorial shows how to reframe landscape footage.

Editing tips for the first three seconds

The opening decides whether people stay. For example, start mid-action rather than with a greeting, show the finished result before the steps, or put a question on screen. In addition, avoid logos and intros at the start of a short: save branding for the end. As a result, viewers see why they should keep watching straight away.

Bonus editing tips: speed, freeze and reverse

  • Speed up the boring part: select a clip and use Clip ▸ Speed/Duration… (⌘R) — 200 % for travel, 400 % for a quick time-lapse.
  • Freeze the big moment: Clip ▸ Add Frame Hold stops the picture on the playhead frame — great with a sound effect and a title.
  • Rewind for effect: Clip ▸ Reverse Clip plays a moment backwards.

Short video editing checklist before you export

  1. Does the first second show the payoff or ask a question?
  2. Are there any pauses left?
  3. Can you follow it with the sound off?
  4. Is the audio even, with music under the voice?
  5. Are faces and text inside the safe zone?

Frequently asked questions

How long should a short video be?

As short as the idea allows. Many successful Shorts and Reels are 15–30 seconds; cutting every pause usually takes a video under a minute.

What is the best free editor for short videos?

Any editor with a timeline, captions and 9:16 export will do. Reelsmith adds auto captions and vertical presets for free, with no watermark, in the browser.

Should I add music to every short?

Not always. Music helps montages; for talking videos, keep it quiet or duck it under the voice.

Put these together and even a simple phone clip feels intentional. Open the editor and try them on your next video.

posts.description: Reelsmith is a free video editor that runs in your browser: a multi-track timeline, titles, color, audio tools and auto captions. No upload, no watermark.
posts.excerpt: Reelsmith brings a real multi-track editor — timeline, titles, transitions, color, audio and auto captions — to the browser, with no upload and no sign-up.
posts.imageAlt: The Reelsmith editor with video, title and caption tracks on the timeline
posts.html:
Reelsmith is a free video editor that runs in your browser. Most online video editors fall into one of two camps. Some are template apps: quick, but you can't really edit. Others upload your footage to a server, make you wait, and add a watermark unless you pay.

Reelsmith takes a different approach. It is a full non-linear editor — the kind of tool editors use every day — that runs entirely in your browser, on your own computer.

What you get in this free video editor

  • A proper timeline with unlimited tracks, ripple and rolling edits, slip and slide, the razor tool and frame-accurate trimming.
  • Titles that look designed: 3D, gradient and two-tone styles, plus word-by-word and letter-by-letter animations.
  • 30 transitions, from a classic cross dissolve to whip pans, glitches and colourful shape wipes.
  • Color grading with curves, color wheels and scopes.
  • Audio tools: normalization, EQ, compression, noise gate, voice effects, sound effects and automatic music ducking.
  • Auto captions in more than 20 languages, generated on your device.
  • Fast export to MP4 or WebM, with presets for YouTube, Shorts, Reels, TikTok and Instagram.

Who this free video editor is for

  • Creators making Shorts, Reels, TikToks and YouTube videos who want captions and titles without a subscription.
  • Students and teachers on school laptops or Chromebooks where installing software isn't allowed.
  • Small businesses editing product videos and ads that shouldn't be uploaded to unknown servers.
  • Editors who know Premiere-style tools and want the same workflow anywhere.

How it works

Modern browsers can decode and encode video with your computer's own hardware through the WebCodecs API. Reelsmith builds a full editor on top of it, so playback, effects and export all run locally. In other words, the website delivers the editor, and your computer does the editing.

Nothing to upload

When you import a video into Reelsmith, it stays where it is on your disk. Your browser reads it, shows it on the timeline and, when you export, writes a new file back to your computer. There is no upload queue, no file-size limit set by a server, and no copy of your footage anywhere else. We explain how this works in Why your videos never leave your computer.

Works on computers, tablets and phones

The same editor adapts to touch screens with gestures and bottom-sheet panels, so you can start a project on a laptop and make a quick fix on a tablet. Chrome and Edge give the best performance; Safari and Firefox work too.

Free, without the catch

There is no account to create and no watermark on your exports. Open reelsmithapp.com and start editing.

Where to start

  • New to editing? Follow Your first edit in 5 minutes.
  • Making short-form videos? Read How to make vertical videos for Shorts, Reels and TikTok.
  • Want subtitles? See How to add subtitles to a video automatically.

Reelsmith is new, and it gets better with your feedback. If something doesn't work the way you expect, or you'd like a feature, tell us with Report a bug or Request a feature.

Frequently asked questions

Is Reelsmith really free?

Yes. There is no account, no trial and no watermark. The site will be supported by ads that never cover the editor.

Do I need to install anything?

No. Open reelsmithapp.com in your browser and start editing.

Can it export 4K?

Yes, MP4 or WebM up to 4K, with presets for YouTube, Shorts, Reels, TikTok and Instagram. See Exporting a video.

posts.title: How to Make Quiet Video Audio Louder (and Clearer)
posts.metaTitle: Make Audio Louder in a Video (Free, Online)
posts.description: Make audio louder in a video: boost quiet speech, normalize loudness to −14 LUFS, even out loud and quiet parts and remove noise — free, in your browser.
posts.excerpt: Boost low volume in a video, even out loud and quiet parts, remove background noise and separate the audio from the picture — free in your browser.
posts.imageAlt: Effect Controls with Volume raised to 180% and a Compressor on a speech clip, music on a second track
posts.html:
A great shot with sound you can barely hear is a common problem with phone and camera footage. Here is how to make audio louder in a video with Reelsmith, from the quickest fix to a polished, even result — free, in your browser.

Quick fix: raise the volume

  1. Click the clip on the timeline.
  2. In Effect Controls ▸ Audio, raise Volume. 100 % is the original level; you can go up to 300 %.
  3. Play it back and watch the meters on the right of the timeline. Keep the peaks below 0 dB — if the top of the meter turns red, the sound is close to distorting.

Prefer exact numbers? Select the clip and press G for Clip ▸ Audio Gain… to add or remove decibels. +6 dB is roughly twice as loud to the ear.

Better: make audio louder evenly with Normalize Loudness

Different clips are often recorded at different levels. Select them and choose Clip ▸ Normalize Loudness…, then pick a target:

  • −14 LUFS — YouTube, Spotify and most online video.
  • −16 LUFS — Apple Podcasts and Apple Music.
  • −23 LUFS — European broadcast (EBU R 128).
  • −24 LUFS — US broadcast.

Reelsmith measures each clip with the standard broadcast method and sets its Audio Gain, so every clip has the same perceived loudness and viewers don't have to keep reaching for the volume.

Boost audio without distortion: even out loud and quiet parts

If some words are loud and others quiet, drag Effects ▸ Audio Effects ▸ Compressor onto the clip. It turns down the loudest moments so you can raise the overall level without distortion. Use Make-up gain to bring it back up.

Tip: Order matters: compress first, then normalize. The compressor evens out the speech, and normalizing sets the final level.

Clean up the sound

Making audio louder also makes the noise louder, so clean it up. In Effects ▸ Audio Effects:

  • High-Pass removes rumble from traffic, wind and handling noise (80 Hz is a good start for voices).
  • DeHum removes the 50 or 60 Hz buzz from electrical equipment.
  • Noise Gate silences the hiss between words.
  • Parametric EQ — lift the highs a little for clearer speech, or cut the lows to reduce boominess.

Work on the audio separately

Video and audio from the same file are linked, so they move together. To edit the sound on its own — for example to boost it, move it, or delete it — select the clip and press ⌘L (Ctrl+L on Windows), or right-click ▸ Unlink. You don't need to unlink just to change the volume, though: selecting the clip is enough.

Tip: Recording a narration? Click the mic button on an audio track to record a voice-over straight into the timeline.

Music under speech

Put background music on its own track, select it and apply Effects ▸ Smart Audio ▸ Auto Duck Music Under Voice. The music dips by 14 dB automatically whenever someone speaks, with smooth fades you can adjust.

Make audio louder on a phone

The same tools work in the mobile editor. Tap the clip, then open the Edit sheet at the bottom of the screen and raise Volume. In addition, use headphones while checking: phone speakers hide low-frequency rumble and make quiet speech sound louder than it is.

A quick recipe for clear, loud speech

  1. Unlink the audio if you want to work on it alone (⌘L).
  2. Add High-Pass at 80 Hz and, if you hear a buzz, DeHum.
  3. Add a Compressor.
  4. Run Normalize Loudness… at −14 LUFS.
  5. Duck the music with Auto Duck Music Under Voice.

Frequently asked questions

How do I increase the volume of a video beyond 100%?

Raise Volume up to 300 % in Effect Controls, or add decibels with Audio Gain… (G). Watch the meters so the peaks stay below 0 dB.

Why does my audio distort when I make it louder?

The loudest moments are hitting the limit. Add a Compressor first, then raise the level, or lower the gain until the meters stop turning red.

What loudness should I use for YouTube?

−14 LUFS. YouTube turns louder videos down to about this level anyway, so going louder only adds distortion.

Is my audio uploaded?

No. All processing happens in your browser on your own computer.

More detail: Working with audio, Audio effects and Detaching audio from video. Clean audio also makes automatic subtitles more accurate.

posts.title: Why Your Videos Never Leave Your Computer
posts.metaTitle: Video Editing in the Browser, Privately
posts.description: How video editing in the browser keeps files private: Reelsmith edits, captions and exports on your own computer with WebCodecs. Nothing is uploaded.
posts.excerpt: How Reelsmith edits, captions and exports video entirely inside your browser — and why that is faster and more private than uploading.
posts.imageAlt: The Reelsmith start screen: open videos from your computer, files stay on your device
posts.html:
Video editing in the browser usually means uploading. "Online video editor" usually means "upload your video to someone else's computer". Reelsmith works differently: it is a website, but the editing happens on your machine. Here's how, and why it matters.

Video editing in the browser: the browser is now a workstation

Modern browsers ship with the building blocks of a video editor:

  • Hardware video decoding and encoding (WebCodecs) — the same video chips your computer uses to play and record video.
  • The graphics chip (WebGL and WebGPU) for real-time effects, color correction and compositing.
  • A professional audio engine (Web Audio) for mixing, EQ, compression and effects.
  • Direct file access — in Chrome and Edge, a website can read the files you choose and save a new file where you say, with your permission.

Reelsmith uses these directly. When you press play, your browser decodes the frames, Reelsmith composites titles, effects and transitions on the graphics chip, and the result appears in the Program monitor. When you export, the same pipeline runs faster than real time and the encoder writes an MP4 straight to your disk.

What video editing in the browser means for you

  • Privacy. Client footage, family videos and unreleased work are never copied to a server.
  • No waiting for uploads. A 4 GB file is ready to edit the moment you import it.
  • No server-side limits. File size and length are limited only by your computer.
  • It keeps working when the connection drops. Once the page has loaded, editing doesn't need the internet.

What about auto captions?

Speech recognition usually happens in the cloud. In Reelsmith it doesn't. The first time you click Generate, your browser downloads an open-source speech model (Whisper) once and keeps it. From then on, your audio is transcribed on your device — it is never sent anywhere. You can remove the model at any time from Captions ▸ Remove Caption Engine.

What is stored, and where

  • Projects you save are kept in your browser's storage on your computer. Use File ▸ Download Project File for a backup you can move to another machine.
  • Your media stays in its original folder. In Chrome and Edge, Reelsmith remembers which files a project uses, so it can reopen them next time after you click Reconnect files.

The full details are in our Privacy Policy.

Private video editing vs. cloud editors

Cloud editors copy your footage to their servers, process it there and send back a result. That is convenient for collaboration. However, it means waiting for uploads, accepting storage limits and trusting another company with your files. In contrast, video editing in the browser with Reelsmith keeps everything on your device. As a result, it suits client work, family videos and anything under an agreement not to share.

The trade-offs

Doing everything locally means your computer does the work. A recent laptop handles 1080p editing comfortably; very long 4K projects are smoother on a desktop with plenty of memory. Chrome and Edge currently offer the best performance and file access; Safari and Firefox work, with exports saved to Downloads.

How to check that nothing is uploaded

You don't have to take our word for it. Open your browser's developer tools (F12 in Chrome or Edge), choose the Network tab, then import and export a video. You'll see the page and its code load — but no request that carries your video. You can even disconnect from the internet after the page has loaded and keep editing.

Frequently asked questions

Can I edit videos offline?

Once the page has loaded, editing and exporting work without a connection. Auto captions need the internet only the first time, to download the speech model.

Where are my projects saved?

In your browser's storage on your computer. Use File ▸ Download Project File to keep a backup or move a project to another machine.

Does Reelsmith use my videos for AI training?

No. Your videos never leave your device, so there is nothing to train on.

Ready to try it? Open the editor — there is nothing to install.

posts.title: How to Remove the Background from a Video or Logo
posts.description: Remove video background colours — white, black or green screen — and make logos transparent in a free browser editor. Step by step, nothing uploaded.
posts.excerpt: Make a white, black or green background transparent — for logos, subscribe animations and green-screen clips — in a free browser video editor.
posts.imageAlt: An overlay with its white background removed, showing the main video through it
posts.html:
Overlay graphics are everywhere, for example: a subscribe animation in the corner, a logo watermark, a green-screen clip of you over a new background. They usually come with a solid background that has to go. Here is how to remove video background colours in Reelsmith in a couple of clicks — free, in your browser.

How it works

Reelsmith removes a background by colour: everything close to the chosen colour becomes transparent, so the video on the track below shows through. This is the same idea as a film studio's green screen, known as chroma keying. It works best when the background is one plain colour that doesn't appear in the subject.

Remove a video background

This works for animations on a white, black or green background, such as a like-and-subscribe clip.

  1. Put your main video on V1.
  2. Put the overlay video on V2, directly above it.
  3. Right-click the overlay clip ▸ Remove Background. (Or select it and click Remove Background in Effect Controls.)

Reelsmith looks at the edges of the frame, detects the background colour and sets up the Ultra Key effect for you.

Fine-tune it

In Effect Controls ▸ Ultra Key:

  • Mode: Brightness for white, black or grey backgrounds; Colour for green or blue screens.
  • Keep inside (edges only): removes only the background that touches the edges of the frame, so white text or icons inside the animation stay visible.
  • Tolerance: raise it if a light fringe remains; lower it if parts of the animation disappear.
  • Softness: smooths the edge.

Place and size it

Use Effect Controls ▸ Motion — or drag the clip in the Program monitor — to scale it down and move it, for example to the bottom of the frame.

Green screen: remove a green background from video

  1. Put the new background (a photo or video) on V1 and your green-screen clip on V2.
  2. Right-click the green-screen clip ▸ Remove Background. Reelsmith picks the green and sets Mode to Colour.
  3. Raise Tolerance until the last green patches disappear, then add a little Softness so hair and edges blend in.

Tip: Light the green screen evenly and stand a step away from it. Shadows and green light bouncing onto the subject are the usual causes of patchy results.

Remove a logo or image background

  1. Import the logo.
  2. Right-click it in the Project panel (or on the timeline) ▸ Remove Background…
  3. The preview shows transparent areas as a checkerboard. Click the preview to pick the background colour, or Shift+click to add more colours for gradients.
  4. Choose Background touching the edges to keep white parts inside the logo, or This colour everywhere to also clear the holes in letters like O, A and e.
  5. Adjust Tolerance and Edge softness, tick Trim transparent edges if you like, and click Remove Background.

A new transparent PNG is added to the Project panel and your clip switches to it. The original stays untouched.

Fixing common problems when you remove a video background

  • A thin white or green outline stays: raise Tolerance a little, then add Softness.
  • Parts of the subject vanish: lower Tolerance, or tick Keep inside (edges only) so only the outer background is removed.
  • The background is a gradient: for images, Shift+click several colours in the preview.
  • The background changes colour in the video: colour removal needs a steady colour; use a mask instead (below).

Remove video background for a logo watermark

A transparent logo in a corner makes your videos look consistent. First, remove the logo's background as shown above. Then place it on the top video track for the whole length of the video, scale it to about 10–15 % of the frame width, and lower it in Effect Controls ▸ Opacity so it doesn't distract. Finally, check it against both light and dark scenes.

When colour removal isn't enough

Background removal works by colour, so it's best for graphics and screens with a plain background. To cut out a person in an everyday photo or video, draw a mask around them and use mask tracking to follow the movement.

Tip: Need a subscribe button and don't have one? The Library tab has animated buttons with transparent backgrounds already — see Add an animated subscribe button.

Frequently asked questions

Can I remove a video background without a green screen?

Yes, if the background is a plain colour such as white or black. For busy, real-world backgrounds, use a mask with tracking instead.

Is my video uploaded?

No. The effect runs on your computer's graphics chip while you edit and export.

Does the transparent part export as transparent?

The transparent area shows the tracks below it, and the exported MP4 contains the combined picture. MP4 itself has no transparency.

More detail: Green screen (Ultra Key) and Remove an image background.

posts.title: How to Make Vertical Videos for Shorts, Reels and TikTok
posts.metaTitle: Vertical Video for Shorts, Reels and TikTok
posts.description: Make a vertical video in 9:16 for Shorts, Reels and TikTok: reframe landscape clips, add captions and export 1080×1920 — free, in your browser.
posts.excerpt: Edit 9:16 vertical videos in your browser — turn landscape footage vertical, add captions and text, and export at the right size for Shorts, Reels and TikTok.
posts.imageAlt: Editing a vertical 9:16 video with a headline and captions in Reelsmith
posts.html:
Short-form platforms expect a vertical video in 9:16 at 1080×1920. Here is how to make one in Reelsmith, whether you filmed vertically or horizontally — free, in your browser, with nothing uploaded.

The right vertical video size

YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels and TikTok all play full-screen vertical video. Use 1080×1920 pixels (9:16), keep it under a minute if you are unsure, and export as MP4. YouTube lists its current limits in Upload YouTube Shorts.

If you filmed a vertical video on your phone

Start a project and drop in your phone clip. In a new sequence, the first video you add sets the frame size — a vertical clip makes a 9:16 sequence automatically. A message confirms it, and ⌘Z (Ctrl+Z on Windows) undoes it.

If you filmed horizontally

  1. Choose Sequence ▸ Sequence Settings… and pick the Vertical 9:16 (1080×1920) preset.
  2. Add your landscape clip. It sits in the middle with empty space above and below.
  3. Select the clip and open Effect Controls ▸ Motion. Raise Scale until the picture fills the height, then drag it left or right in the Program monitor to frame your subject.

Tip: If your subject moves around, add Position keyframes so the frame follows them. See Effect Controls and keyframes.

Or keep the whole picture with a blurred background

Don't want to crop? Apply Effects ▸ Creative Effects ▸ Background Blur Fill. The full landscape picture stays in the middle and the empty space above and below is filled with a blurred copy — a popular look for reposting horizontal clips.

Make your vertical video work without sound

Most people scroll with the sound off. Therefore, on-screen text matters:

  • Auto captions: Captions ▸ Auto-generate Captions… writes subtitles from your speech — see How to add subtitles automatically.
  • A hook in the first second: press T, click the video and type a short headline. Then try a style from Effects ▸ Text Styles and an animation such as Words Pop from Effects ▸ Animations — In.
  • Keep text in the middle: the top and bottom of the screen are often covered by the app's buttons and captions. Click Safe in the Program monitor to show safe margins.

Keep it moving

  • Cut out pauses with the razor tool (C), then delete the gaps (see Deleting clips and closing gaps) so the video never stalls.
  • Use quick transitions like Whip Pan, Zoom In or Flash between scenes, and the Zoom Punch (beat) effect from Effects ▸ Creative Effects for emphasis.
  • Add a sound effect (Effects ▸ Sound Effects) on key moments.

For more ideas, read 7 editing tips that make short videos easier to watch.

Common vertical video mistakes

  • Text at the very top or bottom. As a result, the app's buttons cover it; keep it in the middle.
  • Black bars above and below. Instead, scale the clip up or use Background Blur Fill.
  • A slow first second. Viewers decide fast, so open on the best moment.
  • Exporting landscape by mistake. Check that the export preset says 9:16 before you click Export.

Export your vertical video at the right size

Click Export and choose the YouTube Shorts / Reels / TikTok (9:16) preset — 1080×1920 H.264 MP4. If your sequence is already vertical, Match Source gives the same result. Then upload the file from your phone or computer.

Frequently asked questions

What aspect ratio is a vertical video?

9:16 — nine units wide for every sixteen tall. 1080×1920 pixels is the standard size for Shorts, Reels and TikTok.

Can I make a vertical video from a horizontal one?

Yes. Switch the sequence to the Vertical 9:16 (1080×1920) preset, then either scale the clip up to fill the frame or use Background Blur Fill to keep the whole picture.

Can I edit vertical videos on my phone?

Yes. Reelsmith works in mobile browsers with touch gestures, so you can edit and export on the same phone you filmed with.

Will the export have a watermark?

No. Exports are free and never watermarked.
